answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before bidding and cap influence by stake rather than a claimed name. A glacier of fake agents must tie up capital for every account; audits that prove coordinated duplicate claims let the protocol slash their bonds. The lotus of cheap account creation then buys little extra influence: the attacker bears opportunity cost and risks forfeiture, though a wealthy attacker may still afford it, especially near the nadir of token prices.
